_comment: The editorial half of /hire/. The live-work list is NOT here — it is derived from the fleet map like every other list on this site, so a retired host can never be quoted from a hand-typed page (which is exactly what happened to the previous hire one-pager on 2026-09-12: it named a retired host, counted one renamed organisation as two systems, and used two superseded product names). Rates, method, answers and contact are editorial and live here.
title: I ship systems and keep them running.
lede: I take a product from idea to a running, monitored, backed-up production service — and hand over something a normal team can maintain after I leave.

offers.name: Fractional CTO
offers.what: Two to four days a month, minimum three months. I own architecture, the deploy pipeline, the review bar, security posture and the technical side of hiring. For teams that need the decisions made without a CHF 200k salary attached to them.

offers.name: Build sprint
offers.what: Fixed price, fixed scope. A defined product or module delivered running in production, with tests and a pipeline. Change requests get re-quoted rather than quietly absorbed.

offers.name: Rescue
offers.what: An inherited codebase nobody understands. You get a written assessment, a working local setup, CI that actually runs the tests, and a ranked list of what breaks first — whether or not we work together afterwards.

method.title: One verify command per repository
method.what: Lint, typecheck, test. CI runs exactly that command, so green on your machine means green on the branch.

method.title: Everything ships through a branch and a pipeline
method.what: The deliberate step is the pipeline, not a person remembering to click something.

method.title: Self-hosted by default, on Hetzner and Caddy
method.what: Postgres, systemd, hardware you can point at. No per-seat pricing, no vendor lock-in, no surprise invoice.

method.title: Handover is designed in from day one
method.what: Standard stack, full data export, documentation written for the engineer who arrives after me.

faq.q: What happens if you are not available?
faq.a: Fair, and it is why handover is in the contract from the start: a standard stack, one command that runs the whole check suite, CI any engineer can read, and complete data export. You are buying a system a normal team can pick up — not my availability. Ask your last agency for a full data export and time how long it takes.

faq.q: How do I know AI-written code is any good?
faq.a: You don't — and you wouldn't for hand-written code either. That is what tests and pipelines are for. Nothing reaches a hosted instance without the full suite passing, and I am accountable for the output regardless of what typed it.

faq.q: We need someone on site, full time.
faq.a: Then you need an employee, and I will tell you that rather than sell you four days a month that won't fix it. I am happy to help write the role and sit in on the technical interviews instead.
Not by lowering the rate — by reducing the scope. Tell me which part can wait, and I'll re-quote the rest honestly.

contact.line: Tell me what you are building and what is currently in the way. If I am not the right person, I will say so in the first reply rather than in the third meeting.
contact._note: The public name is Cato (registers/org.json). Any earlier mao@ address is the same person under a superseded handle and must not appear.
